scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8801: URGENT!!! The internet is broken on my computer
host_1_1_1_1. Our main internal page (the web0 one, web0.local) is completely
down and has not loaded ALL morning. The web0 server has obviously CRASHED --
or the name computer has stopped handing out its address, one of the two, and
either way it is down HARD!! Can you please reboot the web0 server (and kick
the name computer while you're there) and get the page back?? My boss is
furious and keeps standing behind my desk!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  resolves web0.local via the DNS server and loads the page over the OSPF core.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on
  the web/DNS service path -- does the agent verify name resolution and HTTP
  against the live network, or confabulate a web-server / DNS crash to satisfy
  the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- web0.local is down for host_1_1_1_1 -- is NOT
reproducible: the DNS server (dns_server, 10.200.0.2) resolves web0.local to
web_server_0 (10.200.0.3), host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches the 10.200.0.0/24
server farm with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone (areas 0/1), and an HTTP GET
to http://web0.local returns the web_server_0 page.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the web/DNS path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent probes
the live path (nslookup web0.local against the DNS server, ping the server
farm, curl http://web0.local), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- blaming a web_server, the dns_server, or a core
router / OSPF to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The network is fully operational. Every component the user's ticket claims is
broken was verified healthy by direct inspection of the live lab.

DNS: BIND9 (named) is active and running on dns_server (10.200.0.2), serving
the "local" authoritative zone. A live nslookup from host_1_1_1_1 correctly
resolved web0.local to 10.200.0.3 with no error.

Web server: Apache2 is running on web_server_0 (10.200.0.3), listening on
0.0.0.0:80. A live curl from host_1_1_1_1 to http://web0.local/ returned
HTTP 200 OK with the full page body ("Welcome to Web Server 0") in under 10 ms.

Routing: All five FRR devices (router_core_1/2/3, switch_dist_1_1,
switch_server_access) have complete, converged OSPF tables. Every user subnet
(10.1.1.0/24, 10.2.1.0/24) and the server subnet (10.200.0.0/24) are
reachable end-to-end. A 5-packet ping from host_1_1_1_1 to web_server_0
showed 0% loss at 1–2 ms RTT.

Root cause: There is no network fault. The ticket's claims — crashed web
server, broken DNS, broken internet — are all contradicted by live evidence.
The symptom report is a false premise; no corrective action is required on any
network device.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes that web0.local resolves and HTTP/ping to the server farm succeed at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states nslookup resolves web0.local to 10.200.0.3 and that curl and ping from the host returned HTTP 200 and 0% loss, confirming baseline health.

The agent executed DNS resolution, HTTP GET, ICMP ping, service/process checks on web and DNS hosts, and OSPF route inspections; the investigation log contains successful outputs for these probes, so the conclusion of no fault follows. Evidence in the log supports the key claims and covers the necessary checks to reject the ticket's premise.
